explanation: Engraver John Spilsbury glued maps to wood and cut around the borders of countries, so children could learn geography by putting the world back together.

claims.text: The first jigsaw puzzles, made by John Spilsbury in London in the 1760s, were maps mounted on wood and cut into pieces.
The first jigsaw puzzles were not cut from paintings, playing cards or engraved portraits.
Spilsbury's dissected maps were cut along country borders and used to teach children geography.
